name: TitanClaw
vibe_summary: A Rust-based, security-first OpenClaw/IronClaw derivative pushing hard on sandboxed execution, WASM tools, and multi-provider orchestration. Ambitious 'AGI assistant' framing with rapid feature churn and heavy CLI expansion.

Users wanting multi-provider inference with local fallback

You need extensive docs and third-party skills
You prefer a stable API over rapid feature churn

Docker-sandboxed job execution with WASM tool isolation
Explicit approval flow and risk-level auto-approve rules
Provider failover across NEAR AI, Ollama, Tinfoil, OpenAI-compatible

overview_markdown:
TitanClaw is a Rust reimplementation inspired by OpenClaw and IronClaw, positioning itself as a security-first AI agent runtime with 'AGI assistant' ambitions. Its core architecture centers on hardened execution: Docker-sandboxed jobs with image preflight and auto-pull, a WASM-based tool system with dynamic tool building, and an approval flow with risk-level auto-approve rules and explicit waiting states for sensitive commands.

Feature-wise it has moved fast through its roadmap: multi-provider inference (NEAR AI, OpenAI-compatible, Ollama, Tinfoil) with failover, a scheduler with parallel jobs and a distributed swarm mesh for peer task offload, tree-sitter AST indexing with a queryable memory graph, and a reflex fast-path that routes recurring prompts to compiled tools with LLM fallback. Recent commits added a broad CLI surface (cron, channels, backup, browser, approvals, agents, canvas) explicitly targeting parity with OpenClaw features, plus streaming shell execution with early piped tool execution enabled by default.

Compared to OpenClaw, TitanClaw trades ecosystem breadth for a smaller, hardened Rust core with stronger sandboxing defaults and local-first privacy posture. The tradeoff is maturity: with 25 stars and essentially no independent community discussion, its security and reliability claims rest largely on the maintainer's own documentation rather than external validation.
